name: Tricuspid Atresia

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Echocardiographic and clinical diagnostic criteria for tricuspid atresia

criteria.description: Complete absence of the tricuspid valve confirmed by echocardiography
Hypoplastic or absent right ventricle on imaging studies
Presence of an atrial septal defect or patent foramen ovale allowing right-to-left shunting
Presence of a ventricular septal defect facilitating left-to-right shunting
Clinical evidence of central cyanosis in the neonatal period

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Echocardiographic confirmation of absent tricuspid valve and hypoplastic right ventricle with evidence of interatrial communication
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is primarily based on echocardiographic findings supported by clinical presentation.

laboratory: Elevated hematocrit due to secondary polycythemia
imaging: Echocardiography demonstrating absent tricuspid valve and hypoplastic right ventricle
Chest X-ray showing cardiomegaly and pulmonary vascular markings
Cardiac MRI for detailed anatomical assessment
genetic: No specific gene identified; sporadic congenital malformation
Possible association with chromosomal abnormalities in some cases
other: Electrocardiogram showing right atrial enlargement and left ventricular hypertrophy

distinguishingFeatures: Presence of malformed but present tricuspid valve
Right atrial enlargement without complete valve absence
Characteristic apical displacement of tricuspid valve leaflets
Atresia of pulmonary valve rather than tricuspid valve
Right ventricle may be hypoplastic but tricuspid valve present

redFlags: Severe cyanosis unresponsive to oxygen therapy
Signs of congestive heart failure in neonate
Progressive hypoxemia with poor feeding and failure to thrive
references: Anderson RH, et al. Paediatric Cardiology. 4th ed. Churchill Livingstone; 2010.
Moller JH, et al. The Pediatric Cardiology Handbook. 3rd ed. Lippincott Williams & Wilkins; 2013.
